prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is the clearest case on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists build bonds. Rational ligand design and a clear mechanistic picture turned aryl C-N bond formation from a forcing, substrate-limited problem into a routine transformation, and over 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial use at pharmaceutical scale make the impact beyond dispute. After reading the openings I would pair it with base editing credited to Liu alone. Several colleagues (Aqvist, Linke, Chabes, Aili) place base editing in their rankings, and Liu is the single clear intellectual driver of the cytosine and adenine editors. It is deaminase chemistry on DNA that gives precise single-nucleotide change, and it reached patients. The two parts are distinct achievements and the three-person cap is respected (Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu).
statement.case_against: Cross-coupling was honoured in 2010, so B053 can be read as an extension of an already recognised field, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precedent that has to be weighed. It also has little opening support outside my own ballot. Base editing follows closely on the 2020 CRISPR prize, clinical safety data are still short, and as a synthetic chemist I must ask what is new chemically: the deaminase is a natural enzyme repurposed and the innovation is largely protein engineering, so it is closer to biology than the core of molecule-making. Pairing two such different parts is a compromise and not a unified citation.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling only seventh, as a mature successor to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and prefers Liu alone for base editing, avoiding overlap with prime editing.
responses.response: I accept the overlap concern but think it overstates the redundancy. The 2010 prize rewarded C-C coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki). C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution, where amide binding and C-N reductive elimination required bulky, electron-rich ligands, and it is arguably more important in pharmaceutical routes than some of the 2010 chemistry. I agree with his Liu-alone attribution for base editing, which I adopt in my second part, and I share his worry about stacking prime editing on the same prize.

responses.point: Aili ranks base editing first and sees it as a chemical solution to a biological problem, but proposes Liu with Kondo and Nishida because of independent cytidine-deconversion work.
responses.response: I take the Kondo/Nishida question seriously, but their Target-AID work is a parallel cytidine editor and did not give the adenine base editor, which has no counterpart. Liu's group made both classes and the general design, so I would credit Liu alone and let the citation say base editing generally. If the committee wanted to include Kondo and Nishida we could not also keep two names for B053 within the cap, which is a real trade-off I would want weighed.

responses.point: Chabes ranks targeted protein degradation first as a designable chemical reaction hijacking ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, with a Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio spanning PROTACs and glues.
responses.response: I find the principle persuasive and keep B034 as my first alternative. My reservation is that approved degrader drugs are absent, as he concedes, and the credit split between PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon glues (Handa) means a trio would honour one arm and leave the other, which is hard for a single citation. I would not oppose it, but I would not put it ahead of two achievements with a long, stable record.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks nanopore sequencing first on a clean physical principle and ranks base editing seventh, and raises the possibility that Bayley may no longer be living, which would alter the configuration.
responses.response: The principle is elegant, but much of the case is sensing and sequencing technology and the credit is spread over five people, with eligibility unverified. I would want that settled before building a prize on it. On base editing I am more favourable than his seventh place, because the underlying transformation is a chemical modification of nucleobases.

uncertainties: Whether Kosugi, and possibly Migita, tin-amide precedent weakens the priority of Buchwald and Hartwig, which I cannot verify from the supplied files.
Whether the committee will accept a second C-N-type coupling prize after 2010, given only two members ranked B053.
Whether base editing is judged distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and sufficiently chemical for this category.
Whether a two-part configuration with a single-person second part can command a majority of five.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B053, B012 or the alternatives. I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Liu; my Masamune (MIT) postdoctoral background is not a connection to any shortlisted candidate.
